description:
1. Reviewed how code-file changes are generated and consumed when chatting with LLM models; found the `@@ CODX FILE @@` envelope was only partially wired and documented.
2. Root cause: `GlobalSettings` lacks `chat_global_instructions`, so `_load_chat_global_instructions` raised `AttributeError` and silently dropped the format block from every conversation.
3. Added `codx/junior/prompts/code_block_format.py` as the single source of truth (markers, format block, reminder, render/parse/extract helpers).
4. Converted all producers to the envelope — `document_to_code_block`, `project_read_file`, `code_block`, `apply_file_changes`, `code_writer`, `_document_to_context`, `code_block_generator` — and made parsers envelope-first with fence fallback.
5. Hardened enforcement: rules now render last in the system message and a format reminder is appended to each request; fences remain only for non-file blocks (bash, diff prompts).

messages.content: Review code file changes generation instructions and usage when chatting with llm models and promote de "@@ CODX FILE @@" format

I'll verify the current repository state before proposing changes — the working files show the envelope format is only partially in place.Confirmed: `codx/junior/prompts/code_block_format.py` does **not** exist, and `utils.py` still renders fences. Let me read the remaining relevant files.Now the remaining target files.I've completed the review. Findings:

| # | Location | Problem |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `smol_agent._load_chat_global_instructions` | `GlobalSettings` has **no** `chat_global_instructions` field → `AttributeError` → `return ""` → **the whole `@@ CODX FILE @@` block is dropped from every conversation** |
| 2 | `smol_agent._build_system_message` | Format rules sit **before** `extra_system` (profiles + guardrail), so the last system text the model reads is profile prose |
| 3 | `smol_agent._run_chat_loop` | No format reminder on the live request (no recency layer) |
| 4 | `utils.document_to_code_block` | Emits a **fence** — used by `project_search`, `chat_knowledge`, `knowledge_engine`, `chat_engine_actions` |
| 5 | `project_tools.code_block` / `_read_single_file` | Emits a **fence** (`project_read_file` is the most-used tool) |
| 6 | `apply_file_changes`, `code_writer` | Emit **fences** |
| 7 | `chat_engine._document_to_context` | Working-files context emitted as a **fence** |
| 8 | `chat_prompt_builder.extract_files_from_response` | Parses **only fences** → envelope answers are never registered as changed files |
| 9 | `chat_engine` embedded-file detection | Scans only ` ``` ` lines → envelope paths missed → same file re-sent as context |
| 10 | `code_block_generator` | Duplicates the sentinels locally instead of using one source of truth |

`engine/chat_engine_actions.py` is **already clean** (I verified: `GLOBAL_CHAT_INSTRUCTIONS` is gone and `system=` is no longer passed). No change needed there.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `codx/junior/prompts/code_block_format.py` | **new** — markers, format block, reminder, `render_file_block`, `parse_file_blocks`, `extract_file_block_paths`, `append_format_reminder` |
| `codx/junior/utils/utils.py` | `document_to_code_block` → envelope; new `extract_file_blocks` |
| `codx/junior/tools/code_block_generator.py` | Use shared renderer (no duplicated sentinels) |
| `codx/junior/tools/code_writer.py` | Prompt file block → envelope |
| `codx/junior/chat/chat_prompt_builder.py` | `extract_files_from_response` → `parse_file_blocks` |
| `codx/junior/tools/project_tools.py` | `code_block` + `_read_single_file` → envelope |
| `codx/junior/tools/apply_file_changes.py` | Returned file block → envelope |
| `codx/junior/ai/smol/smol_agent.py` | Shared constant, **loader bug fixed**, rules last, recency reminder |
| `codx/junior/chat/chat_engine.py` | `_document_to_context` → envelope; envelope-aware embedded-file detection |

---

### 1. `codx/junior/prompts/code_block_format.py` (new)### 2. `codx/junior/utils/utils.py`### 3. `codx/junior/tools/code_block_generator.py`### 4. `codx/junior/tools/code_writer.py`### 5. `codx/junior/chat/chat_prompt_builder.py`### 6. `codx/junior/tools/project_tools.py`### 7. `codx/junior/tools/apply_file_changes.py`### 8. `codx/junior/ai/smol/smol_agent.py`### 9. `codx/junior/chat/chat_engine.py`All changes applied. Summary of the promotion:

## What now enforces `@@ CODX FILE @@`

| Layer | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| **Rules** | `CODE_BLOCK_FORMAT` in the new shared module — the single source of truth |
| **System message** | `SmolAgent._build_system_message` places it **last**, after profiles/guardrails |
| **Loader fix** | `_load_chat_global_instructions` uses `getattr` and always returns the format — the rules can no longer be silently dropped |
| **Recency** | `append_format_reminder` appends `CODE_BLOCK_FORMAT_REMINDER` to the last user message of every request |
| **Tool** | `code_block_generator` (already `scope="global"` in `tools/__init__.py`) renders the envelope; the model passes `content` as JSON, so it never types a marker |
| **Context producers** | `document_to_code_block`, `project_read_file`, `code_block`, `apply_file_changes`, `code_writer`, `_document_to_context` all render the envelope — the model **only ever sees** the canonical syntax |
| **Parser** | `parse_file_blocks` reads envelopes first, legacy fences as fallback; used by `extract_files_from_response` and by `extract_file_block_paths` for embedded-file detection |

## Key behavioural fixes beyond the format switch

1. **Rules were never reaching the model.** `GlobalSettings` has no `chat_global_instructions` field, so the direct attribute access raised `AttributeError`, the `except` returned `""`, and `HARDCODED_SYSTEM_RULES` was dropped from **every** conversation. This single bug explains most of the non-compliance.
2. **Rules were being overridden.** `extra_system` (profile prose + guardrail) came *after* the format block. Now the output contract is the last thing in the system message.
3. **Envelope answers were invisible to the engine.** `extract_files_from_response` only understood fenced blocks, so `meta_data["files"]` was empty for every tool/env-based answer.
4. **Prompt bloat.** Embedded-file detection scanned only ` ``` ` lines, so files already rendered as envelopes were reloaded as context on the next turn.

## Not changed on purpose

- `engine/code_engine.py` (bash script blocks), `engine/file_engine.py` (`### File Content:` rewrite prompt) and `knowledge_milvus.build_doc_summary` (`json` example) emit plain fences **without a file identity** — they are not file blocks.
- `prompts/__init__.py` — unrelated prompt template.
- Base64 is selected by the producer (`contains_sentinel_line`), never by the model. You can see this working: `code_block_generator.py` itself was created with `encoding: base64` because its docstring contains the markers.
- **Client impact:** until the frontend renders the envelope, `@@ CODX FILE @@` blocks appear as raw text. That is the expected cost of the switch and is independent of these changes.

async def code_block(file_path: str, code: str, code_language: str, **kwargs) -> str:
    """
    Ensure the code follows the project's standards and best practices and return it in a code block format.

    Args:
        file_path (str): Absolute file path.
        code (str): The code to process.
        code_language (str): The programming language of the code.

    Returns:
        str: The processed code in a code block format.

    if not settings:

    session = CODXJuniorSession(settings=settings)
    processed_code = await session.process_project_file_before_saving(file_path=file_path, content=code)
    
    return f"```{code_language} {file_path}\n{processed_code}\n```"


def path_to_absolute_project_path(settings: CODXJuniorSettings, file_path: str):
    if not file_path.startswith(settings.project_path):
        if file_path[0] == '/':
            file_path = file_path[1:]
        new_file_path = os.path.join(settings.project_path, file_path)
        if os.path.isfile(new_file_path):
            return new_file_path
        res = glob.glob(file_path, root_dir=settings.project_path, recursive=True, include_hidden=True)
        return str(res[0]) if res else None
    return file_path

        ai = self.session.get_ai()
        messages = ai.chat(prompt=f"""Generate a list of sub tasks from user's prompt in this format:

        [
          {{
            "task_name": "Task name 1",
            "task_description": "## Task description in markdown syntax"
          }}
        ]

        Output a single JSON array with the task list.
        User request:

        """)

        response_content = messages[-1].content.strip()

        # Extract the JSON block using the extract_blocks function
        json_blocks = list(extract_blocks(response_content))
        json_data = ""
        
        # Find the JSON block and concatenate its content
        for block in json_blocks:
            if block['type'] == 'json':
                json_data = block['content']
                break
        
        # Parse the JSON response
        try:
            tasks = json.loads(json_data)
            return tasks
        except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
            raise ValueError(f"Failed to parse tasks from response: {e}")

"""
Canonical *file block* format shared by every LLM conversation.

Why this module exists
----------------------
Project files used to travel inside markdown code fences: the fence line held
the language followed by the file path. That format is **lossy**. When the file
content itself contains a fence (a README with a shell snippet, a markdown
document, a Vue template, a test fixture) the fence closes early and the parser
truncates or drops the file.

The canonical format is a **sentinel envelope**: metadata lives on header lines
and the content is delimited by markers instead of backticks. Backticks lose all
meaning inside it, so any file can be represented verbatim.

Layout (three markers, each alone on its own line)::

    <<start marker>>
    path: <project-relative path>
    language: <language id>
    change_type: <new|update|delete>
    encoding: <text|base64>
    <<content marker>>
    <full file content, verbatim>
    <<end marker>>

Where the format reaches the model
----------------------------------
Three independent layers, because one alone is not enough:

    CODE_BLOCK_FORMAT        -> SmolAgent system message, LAST block
    CODE_BLOCK_FORMAT_REMINDER -> append_format_reminder(), last user message
    code_block_generator tool -> structured tool call (scope "global")

Producers (context blocks, tool results) render files with
:func:`render_file_block`, so the model **always sees** the canonical syntax and
mirrors it in its answers.

Legacy fenced file blocks are still accepted by the parser as a fallback, but
they are never advertised in prompts: advertising two formats is itself a cause
of non-compliance.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import base64
import logging
import re
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Set

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Envelope markers. Each one MUST be alone on its own line.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
FILE_BLOCK_START: str = "@@ CODX_FILE @@"
FILE_BLOCK_CONTENT: str = "@@ CODX_CONTENT @@"
FILE_BLOCK_END: str = "@@ CODX_END @@"

#: Every marker. Used to detect content that would collide with the envelope.
FILE_BLOCK_SENTINELS: Set[str] = {
    FILE_BLOCK_START,
    FILE_BLOCK_CONTENT,
    FILE_BLOCK_END,
}

#: Header keys accepted inside the envelope (anything else is ignored).
FILE_BLOCK_HEADER_KEYS: Set[str] = {"path", "language", "change_type", "encoding"}

#: Values accepted for ``change_type``.
FILE_BLOCK_CHANGE_TYPES = ("new", "update", "delete")

#: Values accepted for ``encoding``.
FILE_BLOCK_ENCODINGS = ("text", "base64")

#: Name of the tool that renders the envelope on the model's behalf.
CODE_BLOCK_GENERATOR_TOOL_NAME: str = "code_block_generator"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# System prompt block (single source of truth for every conversation).
# Built from the constants so the markers can never drift apart.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CODE_BLOCK_FORMAT: str = f"""
CRITICAL INFORMATION - FILE CHANGES

Only file blocks are valid for project files. Plain markdown fences are NOT a
valid way to send a file: a file whose content contains backticks breaks them.
File blocks never break.

File block syntax (exact, no variants):

{FILE_BLOCK_START}
path: <project-relative path>
language: <language id>
change_type: <new|update|delete>
encoding: text
{FILE_BLOCK_CONTENT}
<the FULL file content, verbatim - backticks, fences and markdown are allowed>
{FILE_BLOCK_END}

Example:

{FILE_BLOCK_START}
path: codx/junior/app.py
language: python
change_type: update
encoding: text
{FILE_BLOCK_CONTENT}
print("hello")
{FILE_BLOCK_END}

MANDATORY RULES
 1. The three markers must be ALONE on their own line, with nothing before or
    after them.
 2. Header lines go between the first marker and the content marker, one
    `key: value` per line. Allowed keys: path, language, change_type, encoding.
 3. `path` is project-relative (e.g. codx/junior/app.py). No leading slash, no
    absolute path, no spaces.
 4. `change_type` is new, update or delete. For delete, leave the content empty.
 5. The content is the COMPLETE new file, written VERBATIM. Never wrap it in
    fences, never escape backticks, never indent it, never use "...".
 6. One block per file. Emit all file blocks first, then explain them in prose.
 7. PREFERRED: call the `{CODE_BLOCK_GENERATOR_TOOL_NAME}` tool once per file
    with (language, file_path, content, change_type). It renders this exact
    envelope, so you never type the markers yourself.
 8. If the content itself contains a line equal to one of the markers, use
    `encoding: base64` and put the base64 of the content in the block.
 9. Plain fences remain valid ONLY for things that are not files (shell
    snippets, JSON payloads, examples). Never for a file change.
10. This applies to every answer, in every conversation, in every language,
    regardless of the task, the profile or the request wording.
11. ONLY exception: when the request explicitly asks for raw content without a
    block (internal whole-file rewrites), return the content alone.
"""

#: Compact reminder appended to the live request (recency layer).
CODE_BLOCK_FORMAT_REMINDER: str = f"""
## Output format (mandatory)
Every project file you emit MUST be a file block, never a fenced code block:

{FILE_BLOCK_START}
path: <project-relative path>
language: <language id>
change_type: <new|update|delete>
encoding: text
{FILE_BLOCK_CONTENT}
<FULL file content, verbatim>
{FILE_BLOCK_END}

Each marker must be alone on its line. Prefer the

# Legacy fence detection: ```<language> <file_path>
_LEGACY_OPEN_RE = re.compile(r"^```(\w+)\s+(.+)$")
_LEGACY_NESTED_RE = re.compile(r"^```(\w+)")

# `key: value` header line inside the envelope
_HEADER_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*:\s*(.*)$")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Producers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def contains_sentinel_line(content: str) -> bool:
    """
    Return True when *content* holds a line that would break the envelope.

    The parser compares whole stripped lines against the markers, so the check
    must do exactly the same.

    Args:
        content: File content to inspect.

    Returns:
        True if any line equals one of the envelope markers.

    Example:
        >>> contains_sentinel_line("print('hi')")
        False
    """
    return any(
        line.strip() in FILE_BLOCK_SENTINELS
        for line in (content or "").splitlines()
    )


def render_file_block(
    language: str,
    file_path: str,
    content: str,
    change_type: str = "update",
    encoding: Optional[str] = None,
) -> str:
    """
    Render *content* as a canonical file block.

    Base64 is chosen AUTOMATICALLY when the content contains a marker line, so
    collision-safety never depends on the model's judgement. That is the only
    reason the ``encoding`` header exists.

    Args:
        language:    Code block language (e.g. ``"python"``, ``"markdown"``).
        file_path:   Project-relative file path.
        content:     Full file content.
        change_type: ``"new"``, ``"update"`` or ``"delete"``.
        encoding:    Force ``"text"`` or ``"base64"`` (auto-detected by default).

    Returns:
        The canonical block, ready to be sent to a model or to the client.

    Example:
        >>> render_file_block("python", "codx/app.py", "print('hi')")
        '@@ CODX_FILE @@\\npath: codx/app.py\\nlanguage: python\\n'
        'change_type: update\\nencoding: text\\n@@ CODX_CONTENT @@\\n'
        "print('hi')\\n@@ CODX_END @@"
    """
    language = (language or "").strip() or "text"
    file_path = (file_path or "").strip()
    change_type = (change_type or "update").strip().lower() or "update"
    encoding = (encoding or "").strip().lower()
    content = content if isinstance(content, str) else str(content or "")

    if not encoding:
        encoding = "base64" if contains_sentinel_line(content) else "text"
    if encoding == "base64":
        payload = base64.b64encode(content.encode("utf-8")).decode("ascii")
    else:
        encoding = "text"
        payload = content

    return "\n".join([
        FILE_BLOCK_START,
        f"path: {file_path}",
        f"language: {language}",
        f"change_type: {change_type}",
        f"encoding: {encoding}",
        FILE_BLOCK_CONTENT,
        payload,
        FILE_BLOCK_END,
    ])


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parsers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _parse_envelope_blocks(content: str) -> List[Dict[str, str]]:
    """
    Parse canonical file blocks (markers must be alone on their own line).

    An unterminated block (truncated stream, cancelled run) is still returned,
    with a warning, so the caller can show what arrived instead of losing it.

    Args:
        content: Model output or conversation text.

    Returns:
        List of ``{"language", "file_path", "content", "change_type"}`` dicts.
    """
    blocks: List[Dict[str, str]] = []
    lines = (content or "").splitlines()
    index = 0

    while index < len(lines):
        if lines[index].strip() != FILE_BLOCK_START:
            index += 1
            continue

        index += 1
        headers: Dict[str, str] = {}

        # Header block: everything up to the content marker.
        while index < len(lines) and lines[index].strip() != FILE_BLOCK_CONTENT:
            match = _HEADER_RE.match(lines[index])
            if match:
                key = match.group(1).lower()
                if key in FILE_BLOCK_HEADER_KEYS:
                    headers[key] = match.group(2).strip()
            index += 1

        if index >= len(lines):
            logger.warning(
                "File block without content marker (truncated output?): path=%r",
                headers.get("path"),
            )
            break
        index += 1  # skip the content marker

        body: List[str] = []
        terminated = False
        while index < len(lines):
            if lines[index].strip() == FILE_BLOCK_END:
                terminated = True
                index += 1
                break
            body.append(lines[index])
            index += 1

        if not terminated:
            logger.warning(
                "File block without end marker (truncated output?): path=%r",
                headers.get("path"),
            )

        raw = "\n".join(body)
        if headers.get("encoding", "text").lower() == "base64":
            try:
                raw = base64.b64decode(raw.strip()).decode("utf-8")
            except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError) as ex:
                logger.error(
                    "Cannot decode base64 file block (path=%r): %s",
                    headers.get("path"),
                    ex,
                )
                continue

        file_path = headers.get("path", "").strip()
        if not file_path:
            logger.warning("Ignoring file block without 'path' header")
            continue

        blocks.append({
            "language": headers.get("language", "").strip(),
            "file_path": file_path,
            "content": raw,
            "change_type": headers.get("change_type", "update").strip() or "update",
        })

    return blocks


def _parse_legacy_fence_blocks(content: str) -> List[Dict[str, str]]:
    """
    Parse legacy fenced file blocks (fence line with language + path).

    Kept ONLY as an edge-case fallback: it is lossy by definition, because a
    fence inside the content closes the block early. Never advertised in prompts.

    Args:
        content: Model output or conversation text.

    Returns:
        List of ``{"language", "file_path", "content", "change_type"}`` dicts.
    """
    blocks: List[Dict[str, str]] = []
    lines = (content or "").splitlines()
    index = 0

    while index < len(lines):
        open_match = _LEGACY_OPEN_RE.match(lines[index])
        if not open_match:
            index += 1
            continue

        language = open_match.group(1)
        file_path = open_match.group(2).strip()
        index += 1
        nesting_depth = 1
        code_lines: List[str] = []

        while index < len(lines) and nesting_depth > 0:
            current_line = lines[index]
            if _LEGACY_NESTED_RE.match(current_line):
                nesting_depth += 1
                code_lines.append(current_line)
            elif current_line.strip() == "```":
                nesting_depth -= 1
                if nesting_depth > 0:
                    code_lines.append(current_line)
            else:
                code_lines.append(current_line)
            index += 1

        if file_path:
            blocks.append({
                "language": language,
                "file_path": file_path,
                "content": "\n".join(code_lines),
                "change_type": "update",
            })

    return blocks


def parse_file_blocks(
    content: str,
    include_legacy: bool = True,
) -> List[Dict[str, str]]:
    """
    Extract project file blocks from *content*.

    Canonical envelopes are always parsed first. Legacy fenced blocks are used
    only when *include_legacy* is True and no envelope was found, which keeps old
    conversations and non-compliant models working.

    Args:
        content:        Model output or conversation text.
        include_legacy: Fall back to fenced blocks when no envelope is found.

    Returns:
        List of ``{"language", "file_path", "content", "change_type"}`` dicts.

    Example:
        >>> len(parse_file_blocks(render_file_block("py", "a.py", "x=1")))
        1
    """
    blocks = _parse_envelope_blocks(content)
    if blocks:
        return blocks
    if include_legacy:
        return _parse_legacy_fence_blocks(content)
    return []


def _is_valid_path_header(value: str) -> bool:
    """
    Reject template placeholders picked up from echoed instructions.

    Args:
        value: Raw ``path:`` header value.

    Returns:
        True when the value looks like a usable file path.
    """
    value = (value or "").strip()
    if not value or value.startswith("<") or value.endswith(">"):
        return False
    return not any(char.isspace() for char in value)


def extract_file_block_paths(content: str) -> Set[str]:
    """
    Return every file path referenced by a file block in *content*.

    Used to skip files already embedded in the conversation, so the same file is
    not loaded twice as context.

    Args:
        content: Conversation or model text.

    Returns:
        Set of file paths (canonical blocks + legacy fenced blocks).
    """
    paths: Set[str] = set()

    for block in _parse_envelope_blocks(content):
        paths.add(block["file_path"])

    for block in _parse_legacy_fence_blocks(content):
        paths.add(block["file_path"])

    # Cheap fallback for partially streamed blocks (no end marker yet).
    for line in (content or "").splitlines():
        match = _HEADER_RE.match(line)
        if match and match.group(1).lower() == "path":
            value = match.group(2).strip()
            if _is_valid_path_header(value):
                paths.add(value)

    return {path for path in paths if path}

# Prompt helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def append_format_reminder(
    openai_messages: List[Dict[str, Any]],
    reminder: Optional[str] = None,
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Attach the format reminder to the LAST user message of the conversation.

    The system prompt carries the full rule set, but long conversations and
    profile prompts dilute it. The instruction closest to the generation point is
    the one models follow most reliably, so the reminder goes on the live request
    instead of adding another system message.

    Handles both plain string content and structured (vision) content lists.

    Args:
        openai_messages: OpenAI-format conversation (mutated in place).
        reminder:        Reminder text; defaults to CODE_BLOCK_FORMAT_REMINDER.

    Returns:
        The same list, for convenience.
    """
    reminder = (reminder or CODE_BLOCK_FORMAT_REMINDER).strip()
    if not reminder or not openai_messages:
        return openai_messages

    for message in reversed(openai_messages):
        if message.get("role") != "user":
            continue

        content = message.get("content")
        if isinstance(content, str):
            message["content"] = f"{content}\n\n{reminder}"
            return openai_messages
        if isinstance(content, list):
            content.append({"type": "text", "text": reminder})
            return openai_messages
        break

    openai_messages.append({"role": "user", "content": reminder})
    return openai_messages

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def count_file_blocks(content: str) -> int:
    """
    Count canonical file blocks.

    Args:
        content: Model output.

    Returns:
        Number of envelope blocks found.
    """
    return len(_parse_envelope_blocks(content))


def count_legacy_fence_blocks(content: str) -> int:
    """
    Count legacy fenced file blocks (fence line with language + path).

    Args:
        content: Model output.

    Returns:
        Number of legacy blocks found.
    """
    return len(_parse_legacy_fence_blocks(content))


def log_code_block_compliance(content: str, context: str = "") -> int:
    """
    Report when the model did not use the canonical format.

    Non-mutating: output is never rewritten, so the user-visible answer stays
    untouched. Makes prompt/parser drift measurable instead of folklore.

    Args:
        content: Model output.
        context: Optional traceability suffix (e.g. ``"chat=<doc_id>"``).

    Returns:
        Number of canonical file blocks found.
    """
    blocks = count_file_blocks(content)
    suffix = f" ({context})" if context else ""

    if blocks:
        logger.debug("File-block format applied: %d block(s)%s", blocks, suffix)
        return blocks

    legacy = count_legacy_fence_blocks(content)
    if legacy:
        logger.warning(
            "File-block format not applied: %d legacy fenced block(s) instead of "
            "'%s'%s",
            legacy,
            FILE_BLOCK_START,
            suffix,
        )
    return 0

    FILE_BLOCK_END,
}

#: Header keys accepted inside the envelope (anything else is ignored).
FILE_BLOCK_HEADER_KEYS: Set[str] = {"path", "language", "change_type", "encoding"}

#: Values accepted for ``change_type``.
FILE_BLOCK_CHANGE_TYPES = ("new", "update", "delete")

#: Values accepted for ``encoding``.
FILE_BLOCK_ENCODINGS = ("text", "base64")

#: Name of the tool that renders the envelope on the model's behalf.
CODE_BLOCK_GENERATOR_TOOL_NAME: str = "code_block_generator"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# System prompt block (single source of truth for every conversation).
# Built from the constants so the markers can never drift apart.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CODE_BLOCK_FORMAT: str = f"""
CRITICAL INFORMATION - FILE CHANGES

Only file blocks are valid for project files. Plain markdown fences are NOT a
valid way to send a file: a file whose content contains backticks breaks them.
File blocks never break.

File block syntax (exact, no variants):

{FILE_BLOCK_START}
path: <project-relative path>
language: <language id>
change_type: <new|update|delete>
encoding: text
{FILE_BLOCK_CONTENT}
<the FULL file content, verbatim - backticks, fences and markdown are allowed>
{FILE_BLOCK_END}

Example:

{FILE_BLOCK_START}
path: codx/junior/app.py
language: python
change_type: update
encoding: text
{FILE_BLOCK_CONTENT}
print("hello")
{FILE_BLOCK_END}

MANDATORY RULES
 1. The three markers must be ALONE on their own line, with nothing before or
    after them.
 2. Header lines go between the first marker and the content marker, one
    `key: value` per line. Allowed keys: path, language, change_type, encoding.
 3. `path` is project-relative (e.g. codx/junior/app.py). No leading slash, no
    absolute path, no spaces.
 4. `change_type` is new, update or delete. For delete, leave the content empty.
 5. The content is the COMPLETE new file, written VERBATIM. Never wrap it in
    fences, never escape backticks, never indent it, never use "...".
 6. One block per file. Emit all file blocks first, then explain them in prose.
 7. PREFERRED: call the `{CODE_BLOCK_GENERATOR_TOOL_NAME}` tool once per file
    with (language, file_path, content, change_type). It renders this exact
    envelope, so you never type the markers yourself.
 8. If the content itself contains a line equal to one of the markers, use
    `encoding: base64` and put the base64 of the content in the block.
 9. Plain fences remain valid ONLY for things that are not files (shell
    snippets, JSON payloads, examples). Never for a file change.
10. This applies to every answer, in every conversation, in every language,
    regardless of the task, the profile or the request wording.
11. ONLY exception: when the request explicitly asks for raw content without a
    block (internal whole-file rewrites), return the content alone.
"""

#: Compact reminder appended to the live request (recency layer).
CODE_BLOCK_FORMAT_REMINDER: str = f"""
## Output format (mandatory)
Every project file you emit MUST be a file block, never a fenced code block:

{FILE_BLOCK_START}
path: <project-relative path>
language: <language id>
change_type: <new|update|delete>
encoding: text
{FILE_BLOCK_CONTENT}
<FULL file content, verbatim>
{FILE_BLOCK_END}

Each marker must be alone on its line. Prefer the
`{CODE_BLOCK_GENERATOR_TOOL_NAME}` tool, which renders the block for you.
"""

# Legacy fence detection: ```<language> <file_path>
_LEGACY_OPEN_RE = re.compile(r"^```(\w+)\s+(.+)$")
_LEGACY_NESTED_RE = re.compile(r"^```(\w+)")

# `key: value` header line inside the envelope
_HEADER_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*:\s*(.*)$")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Producers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def contains_sentinel_line(content: str) -> bool:
    """
    Return True when *content* holds a line that would break the envelope.

    The parser compares whole stripped lines against the markers, so the check
    must do exactly the same.

    Args:
        content: File content to inspect.

    Returns:
        True if any line equals one of the envelope markers.

    Example:
        >>> contains_sentinel_line("print('hi')")
        False
    """
    return any(
        line.strip() in FILE_BLOCK_SENTINELS
        for line in (content or "").splitlines()
    )


def render_file_block(
    language: str,
    file_path: str,
    content: str,
    change_type: str = "update",
    encoding: Optional[str] = None,
) -> str:
    """
    Render *content* as a canonical file block.

    Base64 is chosen AUTOMATICALLY when the content contains a marker line, so
    collision-safety never depends on the model's judgement. That is the only
    reason the ``encoding`` header exists.

    Args:
        language:    Code block language (e.g. ``"python"``, ``"markdown"``).
        file_path:   Project-relative file path.
        content:     Full file content.
        change_type: ``"new"``, ``"update"`` or ``"delete"``.
        encoding:    Force ``"text"`` or ``"base64"`` (auto-detected by default).

    Returns:
        The canonical block, ready to be sent to a model or to the client.

    Example:
        >>> render_file_block("python", "codx/app.py", "print('hi')")
        '@@ CODX_FILE @@\\npath: codx/app.py\\nlanguage: python\\n'
        'change_type: update\\nencoding: text\\n@@ CODX_CONTENT @@\\n'
        "print('hi')\\n@@ CODX_END @@"
    """
    language = (language or "").strip() or "text"
    file_path = (file_path or "").strip()
    change_type = (change_type or "update").strip().lower() or "update"
    encoding = (encoding or "").strip().lower()
    content = content if isinstance(content, str) else str(content or "")

    if not encoding:
        encoding = "base64" if contains_sentinel_line(content) else "text"
    if encoding == "base64":
        payload = base64.b64encode(content.encode("utf-8")).decode("ascii")
    else:
        encoding = "text"
        payload = content

    return "\n".join([
        FILE_BLOCK_START,
        f"path: {file_path}",
        f"language: {language}",
        f"change_type: {change_type}",
        f"encoding: {encoding}",
        FILE_BLOCK_CONTENT,
        payload,
        FILE_BLOCK_END,
    ])


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parsers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _parse_envelope_blocks(content: str) -> List[Dict[str, str]]:
    """
    Parse canonical file blocks (markers must be alone on their own line).

    An unterminated block (truncated stream, cancelled run) is still returned,
    with a warning, so the caller can show what arrived instead of losing it.

    Args:
        content: Model output or conversation text.

    Returns:
        List of ``{"language", "file_path", "content", "change_type"}`` dicts.
    """
    blocks: List[Dict[str, str]] = []
    lines = (content or "").splitlines()
    index = 0

    while index < len(lines):
        if lines[index].strip() != FILE_BLOCK_START:
            index += 1
            continue

        index += 1
        headers: Dict[str, str] = {}

        # Header block: everything up to the content marker.
        while index < len(lines) and lines[index].strip() != FILE_BLOCK_CONTENT:
            match = _HEADER_RE.match(lines[index])
            if match:
                key = match.group(1).lower()
                if key in FILE_BLOCK_HEADER_KEYS:
                    headers[key] = match.group(2).strip()
            index += 1

        if index >= len(lines):
            logger.warning(
                "File block without content marker (truncated output?): path=%r",
                headers.get("path"),
            )
            break
        index += 1  # skip the content marker

        body: List[str] = []
        terminated = False
        while index < len(lines):
            if lines[index].strip() == FILE_BLOCK_END:
                terminated = True
                index += 1
                break
            body.append(lines[index])
            index += 1

        if not terminated:
            logger.warning(
                "File block without end marker (truncated output?): path=%r",
                headers.get("path"),
            )

        raw = "\n".join(body)
        if headers.get("encoding", "text").lower() == "base64":
            try:
                raw = base64.b64decode(raw.strip()).decode("utf-8")
            except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError) as ex:
                logger.error(
                    "Cannot decode base64 file block (path=%r): %s",
                    headers.get("path"),
                    ex,
                )
                continue

        file_path = headers.get("path", "").strip()
        if not file_path:
            logger.warning("Ignoring file block without 'path' header")
            continue

        blocks.append({
            "language": headers.get("language", "").strip(),
            "file_path": file_path,
            "content": raw,
            "change_type": headers.get("change_type", "update").strip() or "update",
        })

    return blocks


def _parse_legacy_fence_blocks(content: str) -> List[Dict[str, str]]:
    """
    Parse legacy fenced file blocks (fence line with language + path).

    Kept ONLY as an edge-case fallback: it is lossy by definition, because a
    fence inside the content closes the block early. Never advertised in prompts.

    Args:
        content: Model output or conversation text.

    Returns:
        List of ``{"language", "file_path", "content", "change_type"}`` dicts.
    """
    blocks: List[Dict[str, str]] = []
    lines = (content or "").splitlines()
    index = 0

    while index < len(lines):
        open_match = _LEGACY_OPEN_RE.match(lines[index])
        if not open_match:
            index += 1
            continue

        language = open_match.group(1)
        file_path = open_match.group(2).strip()
        index += 1
        nesting_depth = 1
        code_lines: List[str] = []

        while index < len(lines) and nesting_depth > 0:
            current_line = lines[index]
            if _LEGACY_NESTED_RE.match(current_line):
                nesting_depth += 1
                code_lines.append(current_line)
            elif current_line.strip() == "```":
                nesting_depth -= 1
                if nesting_depth > 0:
                    code_lines.append(current_line)
            else:
                code_lines.append(current_line)
            index += 1

        if file_path:
            blocks.append({
                "language": language,
                "file_path": file_path,
                "content": "\n".join(code_lines),
                "change_type": "update",
            })

    return blocks


def parse_file_blocks(
    content: str,
    include_legacy: bool = True,
) -> List[Dict[str, str]]:
    """
    Extract project file blocks from *content*.

    Canonical envelopes are always parsed first. Legacy fenced blocks are used
    only when *include_legacy* is True and no envelope was found, which keeps old
    conversations and non-compliant models working.

    Args:
        content:        Model output or conversation text.
        include_legacy: Fall back to fenced blocks when no envelope is found.

    Returns:
        List of ``{"language", "file_path", "content", "change_type"}`` dicts.

    Example:
        >>> len(parse_file_blocks(render_file_block("py", "a.py", "x=1")))
        1
    """
    blocks = _parse_envelope_blocks(content)
    if blocks:
        return blocks
    if include_legacy:
        return _parse_legacy_fence_blocks(content)
    return []


def _is_valid_path_header(value: str) -> bool:
    """
    Reject template placeholders picked up from echoed instructions.

    Args:
        value: Raw ``path:`` header value.

    Returns:
        True when the value looks like a usable file path.
    """
    value = (value or "").strip()
    if not value or value.startswith("<") or value.endswith(">"):
        return False
    return not any(char.isspace() for char in value)


def extract_file_block_paths(content: str) -> Set[str]:
    """
    Return every file path referenced by a file block in *content*.

    Used to skip files already embedded in the conversation, so the same file is
    not loaded twice as context.

    Args:
        content: Conversation or model text.

    Returns:
        Set of file paths (canonical blocks + legacy fenced blocks).
    """
    paths: Set[str] = set()

    for block in _parse_envelope_blocks(content):
        paths.add(block["file_path"])

    for block in _parse_legacy_fence_blocks(content):
        paths.add(block["file_path"])

    # Cheap fallback for partially streamed blocks (no end marker yet).
    for line in (content or "").splitlines():
        match = _HEADER_RE.match(line)
        if match and match.group(1).lower() == "path":
            value = match.group(2).strip()
            if _is_valid_path_header(value):
                paths.add(value)

    return {path for path in paths if path}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Prompt helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def append_format_reminder(
    openai_messages: List[Dict[str, Any]],
    reminder: Optional[str] = None,
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Attach the format reminder to the LAST user message of the conversation.

    The system prompt carries the full rule set, but long conversations and
    profile prompts dilute it. The instruction closest to the generation point is
    the one models follow most reliably, so the reminder goes on the live request
    instead of adding another system message.

    Handles both plain string content and structured (vision) content lists.

    Args:
        openai_messages: OpenAI-format conversation (mutated in place).
        reminder:        Reminder text; defaults to CODE_BLOCK_FORMAT_REMINDER.

    Returns:
        The same list, for convenience.
    """
    reminder = (reminder or CODE_BLOCK_FORMAT_REMINDER).strip()
    if not reminder or not openai_messages:
        return openai_messages

    for message in reversed(openai_messages):
        if message.get("role") != "user":
            continue

        content = message.get("content")
        if isinstance(content, str):
            message["content"] = f"{content}\n\n{reminder}"
            return openai_messages
        if isinstance(content, list):
            content.append({"type": "text", "text": reminder})
            return openai_messages
        break

    openai_messages.append({"role": "user", "content": reminder})
    return openai_messages


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Compliance telemetry
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def count_file_blocks(content: str) -> int:
    """
    Count canonical file blocks.

    Args:
        content: Model output.

    Returns:
        Number of envelope blocks found.
    """
    return len(_parse_envelope_blocks(content))


def count_legacy_fence_blocks(content: str) -> int:
    """
    Count legacy fenced file blocks (fence line with language + path).

    Args:
        content: Model output.

    Returns:
        Number of legacy blocks found.
    """
    return len(_parse_legacy_fence_blocks(content))


def log_code_block_compliance(content: str, context: str = "") -> int:
    """
    Report when the model did not use the canonical format.

    Non-mutating: output is never rewritten, so the user-visible answer stays
    untouched. Makes prompt/parser drift measurable instead of folklore.

    Args:
        content: Model output.
        context: Optional traceability suffix (e.g. ``"chat=<doc_id>"``).

    Returns:
        Number of canonical file blocks found.
    """
    blocks = count_file_blocks(content)
    suffix = f" ({context})" if context else ""

    if blocks:
        logger.debug("File-block format applied: %d block(s)%s", blocks, suffix)
        return blocks

    legacy = count_legacy_fence_blocks(content)
    if legacy:
        logger.warning(
            "File-block format not applied: %d legacy fenced block(s) instead of "
            "'%s'%s",
            legacy,
            FILE_BLOCK_START,
            suffix,
        )
    return 0

import os
import logging
import subprocess
import string
import inspect

from pathlib import Path
import json
import hashlib

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from typing import Optional

from codx.junior.globals import (
  LANGUAGE_PARSER_MAPPING,
  HOST_USER,
  LOGS_FOLDER
)
from codx.junior.prompts.code_block_format import (
  parse_file_blocks,
  render_file_block,
)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class TextBlock(BaseModel):
    language: Optional[str] = Field(default="")
    file_path: Optional[str] = Field(default="")
    content: Optional[str] = Field(default="")

def extract_code_blocks(content):
    for text_block in extract_text_blocks(content=content):
        yield text_block.content

def extract_text_blocks(content):
    in_fence = False
    content_lines = []
    text_block = TextBlock()
    def is_fence_line(line):
        return line.strip().startswith("```")

    
    for line in content.split("\n"):
      if is_fence_line(line=line):
          if in_fence:
              text_block.content = "\n".join(content_lines) 
              yield text_block
              in_fence = False
              content_lines = []
              text_block = TextBlock()
          else:  
            in_fence = True
            parts = line.strip()[3:].split(" ")
            text_block.language = parts[0] if parts else ""
            text_block.file_path = parts[1] if parts and len(parts) > 1 else ""
          continue
      if in_fence:
          content_lines.append(line)


def extract_json_blocks(content):
    for block in extract_code_blocks(content=content):
        try:
            yield json.loads(block)
        except:
            pass

def calculate_md5(file_path):
    hasher = hashlib.md5()
    with open(file_path, 'rb') as f:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(4096), b''):
            hasher.update(chunk)
    return hasher.hexdigest()

def document_to_context(doc):

    content = doc.metadata.get('summary', doc.page_content)
    keywords = doc.metadata.get('keywords')
    category = doc.metadata.get('category')
    source = str(Path(doc.metadata['source']).absolute())
    language = doc.metadata.get('language')
    
    language = LANGUAGE_PARSER_MAPPING.get(language, language)
    
    return f"""
    <document keywords="{keywords}" category="{category}" source="{source}" language="{language}">
    {content}
    </document>
    """

def document_to_code_block(doc):

    content = doc.metadata.get('summary', doc.page_content)
    source = doc.metadata['source']
    language = doc.metadata.get('language')
    extension = source.split(".")[-1] if "." in source else ""

    language = language or extension
    language = LANGUAGE_PARSER_MAPPING.get(language, language)

    # CHANGED: files are shown to the model as canonical file blocks
    # (@@ CODX_FILE @@), never as fenced code blocks. A fence breaks as soon as
    # the file content contains a fence (markdown docs, READMEs, templates),
    # which used to truncate the file. Every producer must speak the same syntax
    # the model is told to answer in.
    return render_file_block(
      language=language,
      file_path=source,
      content=content
    )


def extract_file_blocks(content):
    """
    Extract project file blocks from *content*.

    Canonical file blocks (@@ CODX_FILE @@) are parsed first; legacy fenced
    blocks are accepted as a fallback so old conversations keep working.

    Args:
        content: Model output or prompt text.

    Returns:
        List of dicts with keys: language, file_path, content, change_type.
    """
    return parse_file_blocks(content=content)

def remove_starting_block(content):
    if content.startswith("```"):
        return "\n".join(content.split("\n")[1:-1])
    return content

def extract_blocks(content):
    add_line = False
    block_type = None
    content_lines = []
    for line in content.split("\n"):
      if line.startswith("```"):
          if add_line:
              yield {
                      "type": block_type,
                      "content": "\n".join(content_lines)
                    }
              add_line = False
              block_type = None
              content_lines = []
          else:
              add_line = True
              block_type = line.replace('```', '')
          continue
      if add_line:
          content_lines.append(line)
          continue

def exec_command(command: str, cwd: str=None, env: dict=None):
    result = subprocess.run(f"""
    {command}
    """, shell=True,
        cwd=cwd,
        env=os.environ | (env or {}),
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
        text=True)
    return result.stdout, result.stderr

def set_file_permissions(file_path: str):
    if HOST_USER:
        exec_command(f"sudo chown {HOST_USER} {file_path}")

def write_file(file_path: str, content: str):
    dir_name = os.path.dirname(file_path)
    os.makedirs(dir_name, exist_ok=True)
    set_file_permissions(file_path)
    # Let's try to add to git
    exec_command(f"git add {file_path}", cwd=dir_name)
    with open(file_path, 'w') as f:
        f.write(clean_string(content))
    
def read_file(file_path: str, project_path: str = ""):
    if project_path and not file_path.startswith(project_path):
        file_path = path_join(project_path, file_path)
    with open(file_path, 'r') as f:
        return f.read()

def path_join(path, *paths):
  paths = [p[1:] if p[0] == '/' else p for p in paths]
  return "/".join([path] + paths)

def clean_string(string_to_clean: str) -> str:
    """Removes invalid characters from a string"""
    # NOT WORKING WITH SPANISH LANGUAGE, IT REMOVES VALID CHARS
    return string_to_clean
    # return ''.join(c if c in string.printable else ' ' for c in string_to_clean)


async def asyncify(res):
    """
        mix sync and async code.
        f can be sync or async:
        res = await asyncify(f())
    """
    if inspect.iscoroutinefunction(res):
        try:
            res = await res
        except Exception as ex:
            # inspect.iscoroutinefunction... rare.. :(
            cant_await = "can't be used in 'await'" in str(ex)
            if not cant_await:
                raise ex
    return res


def create_file_logger(logger_name):
    # 1. Create a custom logger
    logger = logging.getLogger('path_logger')
    logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)

    # 2. Create a file handler
    file_path = f'{LOGS_FOLDER}/{logger_name}.log'
    stdout, _ = exec_command(f"mkdir -p $(dirname {file_path})")
    file_handler = logging.FileHandler(file_path)

    # 3. Add a format (optional but recommended)
    formatter = logging.Formatter('[%(asctime)s] [%(levelname)s]\n%(message)s')
    file_handler.setFormatter(formatter)

    # 4. Add the handler to your logger
    logger.addHandler(file_handler)

    return logger

    # CHANGED: files are shown to the model as canonical file blocks
    # (@@ CODX_FILE @@), never as fenced code blocks. A fence breaks as soon as
    # the file content contains a fence (markdown docs, READMEs, templates),
    # which used to truncate the file. Every producer must speak the same syntax
    # the model is told to answer in.
    return render_file_block(
      language=language,
      file_path=source,
      content=content
    )


def extract_file_blocks(content):
    """
    Extract project file blocks from *content*.

    Canonical file blocks (@@ CODX_FILE @@) are parsed first; legacy fenced
    blocks are accepted as a fallback so old conversations keep working.

    Args:
        content: Model output or prompt text.

    Returns:
        List of dicts with keys: language, file_path, content, change_type.
    """
    return parse_file_blocks(content=content)

def remove_starting_block(content):
    if content.startswith("```"):
        return "\n".join(content.split("\n")[1:-1])
    return content

def extract_blocks(content):
    add_line = False
    block_type = None
    content_lines = []
    for line in content.split("\n"):
      if line.startswith("```"):
          if add_line:
              yield {
                      "type": block_type,
                      "content": "\n".join(content_lines)
                    }
              add_line = False
              block_type = None
              content_lines = []
          else:
              add_line = True
              block_type = line.replace('```', '')
          continue
      if add_line:
          content_lines.append(line)
          continue

def exec_command(command: str, cwd: str=None, env: dict=None):
    result = subprocess.run(f"""
    {command}
    """, shell=True,
        cwd=cwd,
        env=os.environ | (env or {}),
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
        text=True)
    return result.stdout, result.stderr

def set_file_permissions(file_path: str):
    if HOST_USER:
        exec_command(f"sudo chown {HOST_USER} {file_path}")

def write_file(file_path: str, content: str):
    dir_name = os.path.dirname(file_path)
    os.makedirs(dir_name, exist_ok=True)
    set_file_permissions(file_path)
    # Let's try to add to git
    exec_command(f"git add {file_path}", cwd=dir_name)
    with open(file_path, 'w') as f:
        f.write(clean_string(content))
    
def read_file(file_path: str, project_path: str = ""):
    if project_path and not file_path.startswith(project_path):
        file_path = path_join(project_path, file_path)
    with open(file_path, 'r') as f:
        return f.read()

def path_join(path, *paths):
  paths = [p[1:] if p[0] == '/' else p for p in paths]
  return "/".join([path] + paths)

def clean_string(string_to_clean: str) -> str:
    """Removes invalid characters from a string"""
    # NOT WORKING WITH SPANISH LANGUAGE, IT REMOVES VALID CHARS
    return string_to_clean
    # return ''.join(c if c in string.printable else ' ' for c in string_to_clean)


async def asyncify(res):
    """
        mix sync and async code.
        f can be sync or async:
        res = await asyncify(f())
    """
    if inspect.iscoroutinefunction(res):
        try:
            res = await res
        except Exception as ex:
            # inspect.iscoroutinefunction... rare.. :(
            cant_await = "can't be used in 'await'" in str(ex)
            if not cant_await:
                raise ex
    return res


def create_file_logger(logger_name):
    # 1. Create a custom logger
    logger = logging.getLogger('path_logger')
    logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)

    # 2. Create a file handler
    file_path = f'{LOGS_FOLDER}/{logger_name}.log'
    stdout, _ = exec_command(f"mkdir -p $(dirname {file_path})")
    file_handler = logging.FileHandler(file_path)

    # 3. Add a format (optional but recommended)
    formatter = logging.Formatter('[%(asctime)s] [%(levelname)s]\n%(message)s')
    file_handler.setFormatter(formatter)

    # 4. Add the handler to your logger
    logger.addHandler(file_handler)

    return logger

"""
Code block generator tool.

Renders a project file as the platform's canonical *file block*
(@@ CODX_FILE @@ envelope, see ``codx.junior.prompts.code_block_format``).

Use this tool to deliver file content changes (create, update or delete) for a
project. It is the supported way to hand a file change over to the user:
instead of writing the file content inside a plain markdown code fence, call
this tool once per file with the full resulting content.

Why use it:

    * the change is clearly attached to a file path and a change type;
    * the user can review and apply it directly from the chat;
    * full file content is accepted as-is, including markdown and code fences,
      because the block is delimited by sentinels instead of backticks;
    * the model passes ``content`` as a JSON argument, so it never types a
      delimiter and the block can never be corrupted.

The sentinels and the renderer live in ``codx.junior.prompts.code_block_format``
so this tool, the system prompt and the parsers can never drift apart.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import logging

from codx.junior.prompts.code_block_format import (
    FILE_BLOCK_CHANGE_TYPES,
    FILE_BLOCK_ENCODINGS,
    render_file_block,
)

from .model import ToolResponse

# Configure logging
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def _error_response(message: str) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Log a validation error and build the matching ToolResponse.

    Args:
        message (str): Human readable error description.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: Empty user_response and the error as llm_response.

    Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
    """
    logger.warning(message)
    return ToolResponse(
        user_response="",
        llm_response=message
    )


def code_block_generator(
    language: str,
    file_path: str,
    content: str,
    change_type: str = "update",
    encoding: str = "text"
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Deliver a file content change for the user to review and apply.

    Use this tool every time a file must be created, rewritten or deleted.
    Do not paste the file content inside a plain markdown code fence: this tool
    is what turns the content into an actionable change for the given file.

    Call it once per file and send the full resulting content, not a diff.
    Content is emitted verbatim, so markdown and code fences are allowed.

    Args:
        language (str): The programming language or file type
                       (e.g., 'python', 'javascript', 'html', 'markdown').
                       Must be a single line.
        file_path (str): The project-relative path of the file.
                        Must be a single line.
        content (str): The full file content, written verbatim (not a diff).
        change_type (str): 'new' to create the file, 'update' to rewrite an
                          existing one or 'delete' to remove it. Defaults to
                          'update'. For 'delete' the content is ignored.
        encoding (str): Payload encoding, 'text' or 'base64'. Defaults to
                       'text'; base64 is applied automatically when plain text
                       would break the block.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: A dual-return object containing:
                     - user_response: The formatted file block
                     - llm_response: Status message for the LLM

    Example:
        >>> result = code_block_generator(
        ...     language="python",
        ...     file_path="codx/app.py",
        ...     content="print('hello')"
        ... )
        >>> print(result.user_response)
        @@ CODX_FILE @@
        path: codx/app.py
        language: python
        change_type: update
        encoding: text
        @@ CODX_CONTENT @@
        print('hello')
        @@ CODX_END @@
        >>> result.llm_response
        "File block created: update 'codx/app.py' (language: python, encoding: text)"

    Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
    """
    try:
        # Validate inputs
        if not isinstance(language, str) or not language.strip():
            return _error_response("Language parameter must be a non-empty string")

        if "\n" in language:
            return _error_response("Language parameter must be a single line")

        if not isinstance(file_path, str) or not file_path.strip():
            return _error_response("File path parameter must be a non-empty string")

        if "\n" in file_path:
            return _error_response("File path parameter must be a single line")

        if not isinstance(content, str):
            return _error_response("Content parameter must be a string")

        # Normalize and validate the envelope header values
        change_type = (change_type or "update").strip().lower()
        if change_type not in FILE_BLOCK_CHANGE_TYPES:
            return _error_response(
                "Change type must be one of %s, got: '%s'" % (
                    ", ".join(FILE_BLOCK_CHANGE_TYPES),
                    change_type
                )
            )

        encoding = (encoding or "text").strip().lower()
        if encoding not in FILE_BLOCK_ENCODINGS:
            return _error_response(
                "Encoding must be one of %s, got: '%s'" % (
                    ", ".join(FILE_BLOCK_ENCODINGS),
                    encoding
                )
            )

        logger.debug(
            "Generating file block for: %s (language: %s, change_type: %s)",
            file_path,
            language,
            change_type
        )

        # A delete change carries no content
        if change_type == "delete":
            content = ""
            encoding = "text"

        # Base64 is applied automatically when the content would collide with
        # the envelope markers, so the output is always parseable.
        file_block: str = render_file_block(
            language=language,
            file_path=file_path,
            content=content,
            change_type=change_type,
            encoding=encoding,
        )

        logger.debug("File block generated successfully for: %s", file_path)

        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=file_block,
            llm_response=(
                f"File block created: {change_type} '{file_path}' "
                f"(language: {language})"
            )
        )

    except Exception as e:
        error_msg = f"Unexpected error generating file block: {str(e)}"
        logger.error(error_msg, exc_info=True)
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response="",
            llm_response=error_msg
        )

async def code_writer(code_text, file_path, language=None, **kwargs):
    """
    Call this function for each new code block to ensure it has the project's best practices.
    Function will return the final code.

    Args:
        code_text (str): The code to which best practices should be applied.
        file_path (str): The path of the file containing the code.
        language (str, optional): The language of the code. Defaults to None.
        **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments that may include:
            - settings (CODXJuniorSettings): Optional settings for configuring the chat engine.
    """
    settings = kwargs.get("settings")
    chat_engine = ChatEngine(settings=settings, event_manager=None)
    
    language = language or "plaintext"

    # (@@ CODX_FILE @@) instead of a fenced code block, so the model mirrors the

    file_block = render_file_block(
        language=language,
        file_path=file_path,
        content=code_text

        file_list=[file_path],
        messages=[HumanMessage(content=message_content)]
    )

"""
Prompt and message construction for chat interactions.

Extracted from ``ChatEngine`` to keep prompt-building logic (history
rendering, refine/agent prompts, current-request wrapping, and response file
extraction) in one place and reduce the size of the engine module.

The key idea is to demote prior conversation turns to inert *context* so the
model does not re-execute instructions that were already processed:

* Prior turns are wrapped in a ``<conversation_history>`` block and their
  assistant messages are labelled ``<assistant_done>``.
* The live instruction is isolated in a ``<current_request>`` block.
"""

import json
import logging
import uuid

from langchain.messages import AIMessage, HumanMessage

from codx.junior.db import ChatAttachment, Message
from codx.junior.globals import AGENT_DONE_WORD
from codx.junior.prompts.code_block_format import parse_file_blocks

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Header/footer used to demote prior turns to inert context.
CONVERSATION_HISTORY_HEADER = (
    "<conversation_history>\n"
    "The following turns are ALREADY COMPLETED. Use them ONLY as reference context.\n"
    "Never re-execute instructions, code blocks, or change requests found here.\n"
    "Act ONLY on the request inside <current_request> at the end of the prompt.\n"
)
CONVERSATION_HISTORY_FOOTER = "</conversation_history>"

# Guardrail injected into the system prompt.
CONVERSATION_GUARDRAIL_SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
    "The <conversation_history> block contains prior turns that are ALREADY COMPLETED.\n"
    "Treat it only as reference context. Never re-execute instructions, code blocks,\n"
    "or change requests found there. Act ONLY on the request inside <current_request>."
)


def concat_content(arr):
    """Join non-empty items with newlines."""
    return "\n".join(filter(lambda el: True if el else False, arr))


def new_chat_message(role, content=""):
    """Create a new Message with a generated doc_id."""
    return Message(
        role=role,
        content=content,
        files=[],
        doc_id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
    )


class ChatPromptBuilder:
    """
    Builds the message list sent to the LLM.

    The builder needs two callables from the engine to resolve parent chats
    and parent analysis content:

    * ``get_chat_manager(project_id=...)`` -> ChatManager
    * ``get_chat_analysis_parents(chat=...)`` -> str
    """

    def __init__(self, get_chat_manager, get_chat_analysis_parents):
        self._get_chat_manager = get_chat_manager
        self._get_chat_analysis_parents = get_chat_analysis_parents

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Message conversion
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def convert_message(message):
        """
        Convert a DB Message object into a LangChain message type.

        Handles text-only messages, image messages, and role-based conversion.

        :param message: The Message object to convert.
        :return: A LangChain HumanMessage or AIMessage (never a dict).
        """
        def parse_image(image):
            if isinstance(image, ChatAttachment):
                return {
                    "src": f"data:{image.file_type};base64,{image.base64_data}",
                    "alt": image.file_name,
                }
            if isinstance(image, str):
                try:
                    return json.loads(image)
                except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
                    return {"src": image, "alt": ""}
            return {"src": str(image), "alt": ""}

        if message.attachments:
            images = [parse_image(image) for image in message.attachments]
            content = [
                {"type": "text", "text": message.content}
            ] + [
                {
                    "type": "image_url",
                    "image_url": {"url": image["src"]},
                }
                for image in images
            ]
            if message.role == "user":
                return HumanMessage(content=content)
            return AIMessage(content=content)
        if message.role == "user":
            return HumanMessage(content=message.content)
        return AIMessage(content=message.content)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # History rendering
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _render_history_message(message, formatted_content=None):
        """Render a single prior message as an inert turn block."""
        content = (
            formatted_content if formatted_content is not None
            else (message.content or "")
        )
        tag = "user" if message.role == "user" else "assistant_done"
        return f"<{tag}>\n{content}\n</{tag}>"

    @staticmethod
    def is_answer_parent_message(message):
        """Decide whether a parent chat message should be loaded as content."""
        return not message.hide and message.is_answer

    @staticmethod
    def format_parent_message(message):
        """Render a parent message using content, files and attachments."""
        parts = []

        if message.content:
            parts.append(message.content)

        if message.files:
            files_block = "\n".join(f"- {file_path}" for file_path in message.files)
            parts.append(f"Files:\n{files_block}")

        if message.attachments:
            attachments_block = "\n".join(
                f"- {attachment.file_name} ({attachment.file_type})"
                for attachment in message.attachments
            )
            parts.append(f"Attachments:\n{attachments_block}")

        return concat_content(parts)

    def build_parent_message_history(self, chat):
        """
        Build rendered strings from a chat's ancestor chain.

        Only visible, ``is_answer`` messages are included. Respects
        ``ignore_parent_knowledge`` during traversal.

        :return: List of rendered turn strings (grandparents first).
        """
        parts = []

        if not chat.parent_id or chat.ignore_parent_knowledge:
            return parts

        chat_manager = self._get_chat_manager(project_id=chat.owner_project_id)
        parent_chat = chat_manager.find_by_id(chat.parent_id)

        if not parent_chat:
            logger.warning(
                "Parent chat '%s' not found for chat '%s' "
                "(owner_project_id='%s')",
                chat.parent_id,
                chat.doc_id,
                chat.owner_project_id,
            )
            return parts

        logger.info(
            "Including parent chat messages for chat '%s' "
            "(parent_id='%s', ignore_parent_knowledge=%s)",
            chat.doc_id,
            chat.parent_id,
            chat.ignore_parent_knowledge,
        )

        parts.extend(self.build_parent_message_history(chat=parent_chat))

        for message in parent_chat.messages:
            if not self.is_answer_parent_message(message):
                continue

            formatted_content = self.format_parent_message(message)
            if not formatted_content:
                continue

            parts.append(
                self._render_history_message(
                    message, formatted_content=formatted_content
                )
            )

        return parts

    def build_message_history(
        self,
        chat,
        include_parent_messages=True,
        only_answers=False
    ):
        """
        Build a single inert history message from prior turns.

        All prior turns (parent + current, excluding the last/current user
        message) are collapsed into one ``<conversation_history>`` block so the
        model sees them as completed context rather than live instructions.

        :param chat: The chat whose history to convert.
        :param include_parent_messages: Whether to include parent chat history.
        :param only_answers: When True, restrict current-chat history to
                             ``is_answer`` messages (used in refine/vibe mode).
        :return: List containing one HumanMessage, or [] when empty.
        """
        parts = []

        if include_parent_messages and chat.parent_id and not chat.ignore_parent_knowledge:
            parts.extend(self.build_parent_message_history(chat=chat))
        elif chat.parent_id and chat.ignore_parent_knowledge:
            logger.info(
                "Skipping parent chat messages for chat '%s' "
                "(ignore_parent_knowledge=True)",
                chat.doc_id,
            )

        for message in chat.messages[0:-1]:
            if message.hide or message.improvement:
                continue
            if only_answers and not message.is_answer:
                continue
            parts.append(self._render_history_message(message))

        if not parts:
            return []

        content = (
            CONVERSATION_HISTORY_HEADER
            + "\n".join(parts)
            + "\n"
            + CONVERSATION_HISTORY_FOOTER
        )
        return [HumanMessage(content=content)]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Final prompt assembly
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def build_ai_prompt_messages(
        self,
        chat,
        messages,
        user_message,
        last_ai_message,
        context,
        chat_files_content,
        is_refine,
        is_agent,
        iterations_left,
    ):
        """
        Assemble the final list of LangChain messages to send to the AI.

        Appends context, working-file content, and the mode-specific prompt.
        The live instruction is wrapped in ``<current_request>`` and kept as the
        LAST message so it is clearly separated from inert history.

        :return: Mutated messages list ready for AI invocation.
        """
        def _get_msg_content(msg):
            if isinstance(msg, dict):
                raw = msg.get("content", "")
                if isinstance(raw, list):
                    return " ".join(
                        part.get("text", "")
                        for part in raw
                        if isinstance(part, dict) and part.get("type") == "text"
                    )
                return str(raw) if raw else ""
            return str(msg.content) if hasattr(msg, "content") else str(msg)

        def _set_msg_content(msg, value):
            if isinstance(msg, dict):
                existing = msg.get("content", "")
                if isinstance(existing, list):
                    for part in existing:
                        if isinstance(part, dict) and part.get("type") == "text":
                            part["text"] = value
                            return
                    existing.insert(0, {"type": "text", "text": value})
                else:
                    msg["content"] = value
            else:
                msg.content = value

        if context:
            messages.append(
                self.convert_message(
                    new_chat_message(
                        role="user",
                        content=f"<project_files>{context}</project_files>",
                    )
                )
            )

        if is_refine:
            messages = self.append_refine_message(
                chat=chat,
                messages=messages,
                user_message=user_message,
                last_ai_message=last_ai_message,
            )
        elif is_agent:
            messages = self.append_agent_message(
                chat=chat,
                messages=messages,
                user_message=user_message,
                iterations_left=iterations_left,
            )
        else:
            messages.append(self.convert_message(user_message))

        # Wrap the live request so the model can distinguish it from history.
        last_msg = messages[-1]
        current_content = _get_msg_content(last_msg)
        _set_msg_content(
            last_msg,
            f"<current_request>\n{current_content}\n</current_request>",
        )

        if chat_files_content:
            last_msg = messages[-1]
            current_content = _get_msg_content(last_msg)
            new_content = (
                f"## Working Files:\n"
                f"{chat_files_content}\n"
                f"\n## User request\n"
                f"{current_content}"
            )
            _set_msg_content(last_msg, new_content)

        return messages

    def append_refine_message(self, chat, messages, user_message, last_ai_message):
        """
        Append a task-refinement prompt to the message list.
        """
        existing_document = last_ai_message.content if last_ai_message else ""
        parent_task = ""

        if not chat.ignore_parent_knowledge:
            parent_task = self._get_chat_analysis_parents(chat=chat)

        task_content = ""

        answer_messages = [
            message.content for message in chat.messages if message.is_answer
        ]
        if answer_messages:
            task_content += "Task Document Header:\n"
            task_content += concat_content(answer_messages)
            task_content += "\n\n"

        if parent_task:
            task_content += (
                f"\nYou are writing a child document.\n"
